summary: LEGION-75 at PR https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1035, head 7a612252f49e8b0f8d1266f3312b9d08ab5c0d9c (code commit d5fd3ed8cfd01beffb0fd7bc8ec7f7c101dfa866): changes requested. One correctness class stands: not every failure path of `push-main` goes through `fail_outstanding`, so a red run can still hide the successful publish the spec forbids hiding — `git fetch origin main` failing (the tester's finding; reproduced, exit 128, no ::error::, no job summary) and a modify/delete conflict on the manifest (main deleted it; passes the exact-match gate, `git show HEAD:$manifest` dies, exit 128, rebase left in progress, working-tree manifest truncated to 0 bytes; reproduced), plus the jq / git add / rebase --continue lines in the same block. Everything else verified correct: exact conflict rule (Case 2b aborts), GIT_EDITOR=true load-bearing, HEAD:$manifest rewrite changes only the version (pi_envoy's .omp.extensions rewrite is restored before `tag`), three release.yaml call sites match their jobs' tag dirs, identical-version race ends exit 0, dead-script deletion has no live caller. Review posted as legion-reviewer[bot] in one submission with six inline threads: https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1035#pullrequestreview-5191040117.

keyFindings.description: `git fetch origin main` failing exits 128 under set -e with no ::error:: and no job summary; route through fail_outstanding (`|| fail_outstanding "Fetching main from origin failed on attempt $attempt."`) and add a test case with origin pointed at a nonexistent path asserting non-zero exit, the ::error:: sentence, and the summary file.

Modify/delete conflict (main deleted the manifest) lists exactly $manifest under --diff-filter=U, passes the gate, then `git show HEAD:$manifest` dies: exit 128, no fail_outstanding, .git/rebase-merge left behind, manifest truncated to 0 bytes by the redirect. Tighten the resolvable shape to `[ "$conflicted" != "$manifest" ] || ! git cat-file -e "HEAD:$manifest"`, write jq output via temp file + mv, and guard lines 97-99 (or wrap 80-99) so any non-zero exit routes through fail_outstanding; add a modify/delete test case.
Header's 'Every failure here says…' becomes true once the two blocking threads land; otherwise narrow the sentence.
`git rebase --abort || true` prints `fatal: No rebase in progress?` before the real ::error:: when the rebase failed before starting; 2>/dev/null or abort only when rebase-merge exists. Cosmetic.
Test inherits the developer's global/system git config (commit.gpgsign=true fails the seed commit); export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 for hermeticity. CI unaffected.
Case 1 does not assert that main's other manifest edits survive the resolution (a REBASE_HEAD: regression would still pass); have clone a's bump set another key and assert it on origin/main.

testerFindingDecision: Blocking. Spec requirement 3 ('a red run must not hide a successful publish') is categorical, the script header (lines 28-31) promises it for every failure, the fix is one `|| fail_outstanding` plus a deterministic test, and 'pre-existing' does not carry it: a transient fetch failure against github.com is exactly the red run an operator has to decode.
declined: thermonuclear-code-quality's proposal to replace the rebase with `git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD` + re-commit: the spec's Rejected section already rules it out (cannot tell a real divergence from a clean run). Not a finding.
